findings.title: refund() is a get-then-put TOCTOU → concurrent double refund at the gateway
findings.detail: refund() has no idempotency claim and no atomic counter (unlike settle()). The outstanding guard reads inv.refunded_minor, then calls gw.refund(), then does inv.refunded_minor = read + amt.
findings.failure_scenario: Two concurrent refund calls on a paid invoice both read refunded_minor=0, both pass the >outstanding check, both call gw.refund() — customer refunded twice; one write lost so refunded_minor understates.
findings.fix: Claim self._idempo.claim(f'refund:{payment_id}:{amt}') and/or accumulate refunded_minor via incr_if_below bounded by total_minor; call gateway only for the delta that atomically applied.

findings.title: wallet top-up gateway idempotency key omits fund; app claim key includes it
findings.detail: Gateway key f'topup:{tenant}:{payment_token}:{total}' (no fund) at :833 vs app claim key f'topup:{tenant}:{payment_token}:{total}:{fund}' at :848.
findings.failure_scenario: Same token+amount top-up to fund A then fund B in the gateway idempotency window: gateway dedupes (charges once, returns ok for B) but app claim differs (fund B) so it mints a second invoice and credits fund B — charged once, two funds credited (free stored value). Symmetric double-charge if a gateway ignores idempotency_key.
findings.fix: Include fund in the gateway idempotency key so both keys describe the same operation identity.

findings.title: consolidated active-mode groups wallet-pinned + card subs into one invoice charged to one method
findings.detail: _group_gateway_key returns '' for all subs in active mode; _charge_from_wallet opts in on sub.payment_gateway=='wallet' independent of mode, so a wallet sub and card subs land in one consolidated group charged via claimed[0][0].
findings.failure_scenario: renewal_invoice_mode=consolidated + renewal_gateway_mode=active + wallet_renewal_enabled: whole group debited from wallet (or wallet sub charged to a card) depending on claimed[0]; wallet-insufficient suspends the whole group.
findings.fix: Include the wallet opt-in in the grouping key regardless of mode (group wallet subs separately), or refuse to consolidate wallet-pinned subs.

findings.title: reverse_settlement re-introduces the lost-update on settled_minor/status settle() avoids
findings.detail: Reversal writes inv.settled_minor = settled_after and inv.status = 'open' from a read value — exactly what settle() refuses at :1561-1567.
findings.failure_scenario: Reversal racing a settlement (or two reversals): last writer wins with a stale value; persisted inv.status/settled_minor diverge from the atomic counter that invoice_state() uses; dunning/finance read the row.
findings.fix: In reversal don't write settled_minor from a read; derive status from the counter, or gate the row write behind the closed:{inv.id} claim.

findings.title: run_overage aggregates the wrong period window relative to run_cycle's period advance
findings.detail: run_overage reads sub.current_period_start/end (already advanced by run_cycle) and keys overage:{sub}:{period} off current_period_start.
findings.failure_scenario: If run_cycle advances the period before run_overage in the sweep, overage aggregates the next (empty) window and bills zero (revenue leak); across boundaries the same usage can fall into two overage keys.
findings.fix: Bill overage against an explicit closed period captured before the advance, keyed to that period.

findings.title: usage consume _IDEMPO retry-cache non-atomic: concurrent same-key double-fire over-meters
findings.detail: The incr_if_below counter is atomic but the _IDEMPO get/put straddle it (accepted-risk, documented). Round-1 documented exemption; re-affirmed here.
findings.failure_scenario: Two concurrent deliveries of the same at-least-once event with the same idempotency_key both miss prior, both pass incr_if_below, both count — for allow_and_bill this bills the duplicate as real overage.
findings.fix: Claim the idempotency key atomically (CAS put-if-absent) before the counter increment; refund the counter if the claim loses. Or re-affirm the accepted risk.

findings.title: partial refund sets pay.status='refunded', blocking a later full-refund webhook from voiding
findings.detail: Any partial refund() sets pay.status='refunded'; _apply_outcome's 'refund' branch is guarded by pay.status != 'refunded' at :2065-2081, so a later gateway refund webhook is skipped.
findings.failure_scenario: Partial 30% refund via API, then merchant refunds remaining 70% at the gateway; webhook skipped; invoice never flips to void, refunded_minor stuck at 30%, grant not fully clawed back.
findings.fix: Decide refund effect from amount-based inv.refunded_minor vs total, not a binary pay.status.

explored_note: 7 real candidates (not padded to 20). Verified-clean round-1 fixes: atomic invoice-number sequence, cycle/consolidated/overage/webhook use atomic IdempotencyStore.claim, consolidated never sums two currencies, coupon redeem is a real CAS, discount MAX-composition capped at subtotal, entitlement resolver fails closed on lapsed periods, route IDOR guards present, empty webhook secret fails closed, memory/postgres incr_if_below agree.
